source_manifest.selection: First unique documents in pinned source order; alternating validation/test documents

source_manifest.supervision: Self-supervised reconstruction; original spans are not verified corrections
source_manifest.deduplication: Normalized exact window hashes across splits; no general near-deduplication claim

procedural_manifest.provenance: Procedural rule-checked synthetic contrasts; no model teacher; no human labels.

source_corpus.provenance: Procedural rule-checked synthetic contrasts; no model teacher; no human labels.

mining.label_rule: Closed-world exact accepted list; not human judged. Training split only.

corpus.provenance: Mixed procedural contrasts and synthetic TinyStories excerpts; no human preference labels.
corpus.license: Corpus excerpts CDLA-Sharing-1.0; procedural material Apache-2.0.
corpus.deduplication: Exact normalized natural excerpts across splits; original source document splits retained. No near-duplicate claim.

blending.selection: Validation top1 improvement with no top1 loss in either corpus or procedural domain; ties prefer lower weight.

calibration.method: Grid search on validation only: maximize balanced success subject to <=5% clean edits and <=10% wrong edits on errors.
calibration.limitations: Finite synthetic validation; thresholds are not guarantees on user text.

bootstrap.limitations: Within this procedural test; does not measure real-world validity.

case.text: Lily lost her favorite toy. She felt happy. Tears ran down her face.
Ben won the game. He felt sad. He smiled and cheered.
A loud crash woke Mia. She felt calm. Her hands shook with fear.
Sam had not eaten all day. He felt full. His stomach growled.
The baby had played for hours. She felt awake. She yawned and closed her eyes.
Dad came home with a puppy. Ana was angry. She smiled and hugged her new pet.
Mia had a blue cup. She drank from her red cup. It was the same blue cup.
Ben put on his red hat. His green hat kept his head warm. He loved its red color.
The dog chased a ball. It picked up the book in its mouth and brought the ball back.
Lucy planted a seed. She watered the stone every day until the seed began to grow.
Tom opened his book. He read the shoe until he reached the last page.
Mom baked a cake. She cut the chair into slices and served the cake.
The box was empty. There was something inside. It contained nothing at all.
The rain soaked his coat. His coat was dry. Water dripped from it.
The fire went out. The room grew hot. Everyone needed a blanket.
Dad turned off the only lamp. The room became bright. Nobody could see in the dark.
The door was locked. Mia could open it. She needed the key first.
Lucy gave away all her cookies. She had many cookies left. Her plate was empty.
The children stayed inside the house. They played outside all afternoon without leaving the house.
Tom put his toy under the bed. Later he found it on the bed, exactly where he had left it.
The bird sat in its nest. It stayed in the pond all night and left the nest at dawn.
The fish lived in a pond. It swam in the sky while the other fish watched.
Mia hid the key in her pocket. She reached into her shoe and took the key out of her pocket.
The children sat at a table. Their plates were on the floor. They ate from the table.
Lily was a little girl. He put on her coat and went out.
Tom was a little boy. She picked up his toy and smiled.
Two girls went to the park. She played together until it was time to go home.
The puppy was a small dog. The cat wagged its tail and barked.
Mia and Ben were friends. He both liked the same game.
The bird built a nest. The fish laid an egg in its nest.
Yesterday, Tom walk to the park. He stayed there all afternoon.
Every morning, she eat her breakfast before school.
There was three apples on the table.
The two dogs was playing together in the garden.
Yesterday, Mia go home after school.
He gave me a apple. I ate the apple.

previous_ranker_matched_pool.candidate_pool: exact stored candidate pool shared with NLL and v3; no regeneration

limits: TinyStories is synthetic. No human preference labels.
Corpus metric is original-span reconstruction, not semantic correctness.
Procedural cases are the previous benchmark reused for regression tracking.
Legacy probes are repeated diagnostics, not a new unseen test.
